name: Volume Shadow Copies (VSS)
os_min: Windows XP / Server 2003 (Volume Shadow Copy Service and vssadmin); the Explorer 'Previous Versions' / System Protection restore-point workflow used since Windows Vista
location: Mounted via device paths such as \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy<N>; the change-block storage for a volume's shadow copies is kept in the hidden System Volume Information\ directory on that same volume
purpose: A Windows service that creates point-in-time snapshots of a volume, used by System Restore, backup software, and Explorer's 'Previous Versions' feature. Forensically, a mounted shadow copy lets an investigator browse a volume's file system and registry hives exactly as they existed at an earlier point in time, recovering files and hive states since deleted or modified on the live volume.
key_fields: Shadow copy set ID and creation timestamp, from `vssadmin list shadows`
Originating volume and the resulting shadow copy device path
Full file-system tree captured inside each snapshot, including files since deleted, modified, or overwritten on the live volume
Prior versions of registry hives (SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, SAM, NTUSER.DAT) captured inside each snapshot
normal_baseline: A small number of shadow copies per volume on systems with System Restore/System Protection enabled, created periodically or before driver/OS updates. On many hardened enterprise builds and some consumer configurations, System Restore is disabled entirely and no shadow copies exist at all, which is itself unremarkable.
anomalies: All shadow copies for a volume deleted immediately prior to or during a suspected ransomware or destructive-attack timeframe
Command-line or process telemetry showing `vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet`, `wmic shadowcopy delete`, or a PowerShell `Get-CimInstance Win32_ShadowCopy | Remove-CimInstance` invocation
Shadow copy storage association resized to an unusually small maximum via `vssadmin resize shadowstorage`, causing older snapshots to be silently pruned

diskshadow.exe (a legitimate, Microsoft-signed backup utility) invoked interactively or via script outside of any known backup job - a common technique used to delete shadow copies while evading vssadmin-specific detection rules
A shadow-copy-capable volume showing zero shadow copies on a host where organizational baseline/policy expects System Protection to be enabled
anti_forensic_notes: Deleting the VSS catalog via vssadmin, WMI, or diskshadow removes the enumerable shadow copy set, but the underlying change-block data in System Volume Information is not necessarily zeroed and may still be recoverable through raw carving until overwritten by subsequent disk activity. Because VSS deletion is a near-universal precursor to ransomware detonation, its presence is high-signal - but a system where System Restore was already disabled will show no shadow copies for entirely benign reasons, so absence alone should not be conflated with an attacker's deletion without corroborating command-line or event evidence.
